**Chapter 11**

**11.1 Preparation of Aldehyde**

Addition of water: Ethanal is produced when solution of 20% sulfuric acid and 2% mercuric sulfate are added to Ethyne at 80°C temperature.

**Chemical Equation:**

CH≡CH + H2O → 20% H2SO4, 2% HgSO4 → CH3CHO Ethanal

**11.2 Formalin**

Formalin: 40% of the liquid solution of formaldehyde is called formalin. Formalin contains 40% Methanol and 60% water. Formalin is widely used in laboratories. It is used for preserving the dead bodies of different animals.

**11.3 Organic acid or Fatty Acid**

The compounds which have carboxylic group (-COOH) are called Organic acids or Fatty Acids. General formula of fatty acid is CnH2n+1COOH. It is symbolized by R-COOH in short.

**Naming:**

Fatty Acids are named by omitting 'e' and adding (oic acid) with the names of Alkanes. Example: Ethanoic acid.
